text: Every real villain needs a signature doomsday weapon, like an orbital death laser or a hurricane machine. Unfortunately, the laws of thermodynamics do not care about your evil speech.
A laser strong enough to melt a city block or steer a storm requires gigawatts of continuous electricity. That is roughly the full output of an entire nuclear power plant running nonstop.

The instant you flip the switch, your local electric company detects a massive grid spike, assumes a substation is on fire, and remotely shuts off your power. Meanwhile, your mirrors and capacitors overheat past two thousand degrees and melt.

Plus, where did you buy five hundred tons of weapons-grade optics, liquid nitrogen, and high-voltage transformers? Every specialized manufacturer automatically reports bulk orders straight to federal regulators.
Before you can even aim at the moon, your terrifying death ray trips a neighborhood breaker and leaves you sitting in the dark next to a lukewarm toaster.
